dimensions.feedback: The flavor profile is excellent and makes perfect culinary sense. Using a touch of extra-virgin olive oil for a stovetop oat crisp is a great, heart-healthy technique that pairs well with the nuts and warm spices.
Perfect consistency. Every ingredient listed in the header is used properly in the steps.

Fits the Modern American style well. A skillet fruit crisp is a classic, casual American dessert.
Using a stovetop skillet to first toast the crisp topping and then reduce the berries is a highly efficient, suitable method that avoids turning on the oven for a quick dessert.
The computed nutrition is highly plausible and perfectly aligned with the ingredient quantities.
The title and intro are warm, accurate, and completely free of disallowed health claims or 'diet' language.
Highly appealing. It delivers the comfort of a baked fruit crumble in a fraction of the time, making it an ideal weeknight dessert.

Genuinely answers to both conditions: it uses a high-quality fiber source (oats and almonds), heart-healthy fat (olive oil), and a solid protein base (Greek yogurt) without relying on heavy saturated fats.

Excellent balance. The added sugar is incredibly low (just 1/2 tsp maple syrup per serving), relying on whole fruit and spices for sweetness. It still provides a quality carbohydrate serving (22.7g) from the berries, oats, and yogurt.

Spot-on for the Desserts chapter. It perfectly hits the target nutrient tier (carbs in the 14-28g window, >4g protein, low sat fat, <7g added sugar) and delivers the fruit-and-dairy-forward style requested.
Easily achievable in under 15 minutes. All ingredients are inexpensive, everyday supermarket staples.
